title: September DMI gave no clear added upper-third rain probability skill in eight East Africa cells in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether September DMI improves upper-third October-December rain probabilities in eight East Africa GPCP cells. Expanding logistic models used earlier years from 1979 and scored 2000-2025. The baseline used September local rain, Nino 3.4 and a trend. Adding DMI reduced wet-event Brier loss by 6.09%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -3.23% to +14.18%. The wet-minus-dry absolute loss reduction was 0.00719, with an interval of -0.00694 to +0.02087. Both intervals include zero. The test gives no clear added wet skill or wet-dry difference under these models. Only 26 test years, related cells, revised data and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Original code, aggregate scores, bootstrap statistics, a figure, source hashes and an external-data recipe are included. Source records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Mean wet and dry Brier losses and added DMI skill in 2000-2025. Conditional three-year block intervals include zero for both targets.
